answer: A head is paid only if it settles against a one-time gift from the donor nebula: a real donor's matched blood or tissue sample, catalogued on the registry's ledge like a seed lot, usable once, burned on use, bound to one address. Each head claims one star from the nebula, so a farm's tenth head must recruit a tenth human, and every gift spent ripples outward, thinning what its siblings can pull and lowering the zenith they must reach. Tissue-matching makes the marginal donor the rarest type, and one donor's samples share a signature, exposing heads that share a family.
